subject.title: RFC 0024: Localization Runtime and Product Coverage

question: Should OpenClaw adopt RFC 0024's shared localization contracts—especially additive Gateway metadata, recipient-locale ownership, and release-completeness governance—as the product direction for the linked implementation stack?
rationale: The PR intentionally introduces broad API, behavior, ownership, and release-policy commitments; source review cannot determine which compatibility and governance commitments the project wants to make.

options.title: Sponsor a narrowed v1 contract
options.body: Approve the bounded locale-resolution and additive compatibility principles, while assigning owners to settle Gateway inventory, channel recipient locale, and safety-copy approval before implementation merges.

options.title: Request an RFC revision first
options.body: Ask the author to reduce the proposal to the decisions maintainers are ready to own and move unresolved coverage or governance commitments into follow-up RFCs.

options.title: Decline the direction for now
options.body: Keep the current localized surfaces and revisit a shared runtime only when an owner-sponsored implementation need establishes the required contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrowed v1 contract
recommendation.body: Approve the bounded locale-resolution and additive compatibility principles, while assigning owners to settle Gateway inventory, channel recipient locale, and safety-copy approval before implementation merges.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor authored the current RFC and has the most direct context to incorporate an owner-sponsored narrowing or revision; a repository product owner must make the final direction decision.
